summary: THE PILOT IS MEASURED, ON EVERY INSTANCE. cecad.meshfeatures.features() read 11 pilot holes of this size across Pollen's meshes, 8 at Ø2.05 mm and 3 at Ø2.10 mm. The accept band in mate.py (PILOT_MEASURED_MIN/MAX_MM) IS that measured spread, not a tolerance class — a printed hole has no ISO class and none is claimed. Artifact: evidence/pilot-measurements.json, extracted from ce-designs/microduck/out/fasteners/features-by-mesh.json; the per-run grip and pilot depth this connection needs come from out/fasteners/runs.json.

SOFTWARE SELF-TEST, not a bench test, and the ledger vocabulary has no kind for it so it is filed as 'use' and labelled here rather than claimed as 'bench'. mate() SELF-TEST: 13 PASS / 0 FAIL. 7 assertions on what it returns (adds exactly the screw, tight leaves no DOF, loose leaves one helical DOF, the length window is [grip + 1.5 d, grip + measured pilot depth], strip load refused, re-insertions refused, side B claims NO thread designation) and 6 REFUSALS it must make: a thread_int record (that is a CUT thread and a different folder), a pilot with no diameter, a pilot 0.5 mm oversize, a pilot 0.5 mm undersize, an unmapped screw provider, a tapped_hole provider. Every refusal has been seen to fire.

THE HOLDING IS UNMEASURED AND STAYS SO. Four numbers refused: preload, tightening torque, strip/pull-out load of a M2.5 screw thread-formed in FDM PLA at a Ø2.05 pilot, and how many re-insertions the formed thread survives. connection.json record.open_questions names the bench test for each — one afternoon with printed coupons, a torque screwdriver and a force gauge, n >= 5. Until then this folder's verdict is CANNOT DETERMINE and no plastics-handbook figure is borrowed in its place: the resin, layer height, wall count and infill behind such a figure are not ours.

NO HEAT-SET INSERT IS MODELLED, and the refusal is measured rather than assumed. The replica author RECOMMENDS 60 M2 heat-set inserts (fastener-reconstruction.en.md:90). Of 355 holes measured on the reference meshes exactly 3 read as an insert seat by diameter, and all 3 are refuted by their own depth: left_shell idx6 Ø4.088 x 29.265 mm deep is a boss channel, yaw_roll_motion idx12/13 Ø4.6 x 0.500 mm deep are lead-in chamfers. A real M2/M2.5 insert seat is 4-6 mm deep. No insert part was created and none placed. What settles it: a teardown photograph of a boss on a real unit, or a caliper on one.

compat() SELF-TEST: 12 PASS / 0 FAIL. It grades what CAN be graded (interface names, screw size, pilot diameter against the MEASURED band, engagement between the 1.5 d rule and the measured pilot depth, both providers) and it CANNOT RETURN PASS for a real pair, by construction: the 'holding' check is always CANNOT DETERMINE because nobody has pulled this screw out of this pilot. The test asserts exactly that — a fully-stated good pair comes back CANNOT DETERMINE and the only non-PASS check is 'holding' — plus 6 FAIL cases (thread_int record, oversize pilot, wrong size, a screw that bottoms, a screw too short to engage, an unmapped provider) and an empty pair that is CANNOT DETERMINE rather than FAIL. The accept band is RE-DERIVED from the listed measurements at test time, so the two constants cannot drift from the data.
